newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Next says sales, market share up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Next says sales, market share up.

text.p: British fashion and home shopping retailer retailer Next Plc said on Wednesday sales had been strong so far in its current financial year and its market share was increasing.
Chief executive David Jones said the group's retail and directory mail order businesses were doing pretty well.
"The fact that we are increasing our turnover at a higher rate than the rest of the trade means we are taking market share," he said in an interview.
He said the situation with Next's four stores in the United States was improving. "It's not earth shattering, but it's improving."
The group was looking at replacing one of its U.S. stores with a better site, but had no plans for major expansion.
"Our policy in America is to keep working at it...but I mean we're not going to go mad and invest a huge amount of money until such time as we're absolutely certain it's the right thing to do."
The group has 30 franchise stores in Europe, Far East and Middle East and hopes to open another 15 this year.
Jones said Next would continue to invest its cash surplus in the business, including personal loans, its Next Directory credit business and stock.
There were no plans for major acquisitions. "I have no grand designs," Jones said.

He also said there were no plans for any tie-up with Great Universal Stores Plc, whose chairman Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale, is also chairman of Next. "I think that there is nothing on the horizon whatsoever."
Next earlier reported annual pretax profits of 158.8 million stg, at the top end of market expectations. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
